newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian stevedores say could strike again soon.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian stevedores say could strike again soon.

text.p: Stevedores at the key Brazilian port of Santos are ready to go back on strike immediately should steel company Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) start loading vessels at its private terminal, a spokesman said.
"If they start operating the strike would be immediate," said National Dockworkers' Union president Abelardo Fernandes.

Stevedores at Santos went on strike for three days last week over a ruling which allowed Cosipa workers to conduct loading and unloading at its terminal. Unions say only qualified stevedores should be allowed to operate there.

Any fresh stoppage could again spread to national level, as did the Santos port strike last week which also affected other commodities ports such as Vitoria and Rio de Janeiro, although grain loading at the key port of Paranagua was not affected.
"Initially it would be in Santos but it could become national," said Fernandes.
Twenty-six stevedores are still occupying two vessels at the Cosipa terminal while military police officers were inside the terminal, the port authority said.
The stevedores will remain inside the ships until talks with Cosipa begin, said Fernandes, adding so far no negotiations had taken place.
A spokeswoman for the steel company said it was holding an internal meeting to set out its position.
